9 A curve which passes through  $ (0, 3) $ has equation  $ y = \mathrm{f}(x) $. It is given that  $ \mathrm{f}'(x) = 1 - \frac{2}{(x-1)^{3}} $.

(a) Find the equation of the curve. [4]

The tangent to the curve at  $ (0, 3) $ intersects the curve again at one other point, P.

(b) Show that the x-coordinate of P satisfies the equation  $ (2x+1)(x-1)^{2} - 1 = 0 $. [4]

(c) Verify that  $ x = \frac{3}{2} $ satisfies this equation and hence find the y-coordinate of P. [2]
